title: 2016 AMC 12A Problem 12
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=6,\) \(BC=7,\) and \(CA=8.\) Point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{BC},\) and \(\overline{AD}\) bisects \(\angle BAC.\) Point \(E\) lies on \(\overline{AC},\) and \(\overline{BE}\) bisects \(\angle ABC.\) The bisectors intersect at \(F.\) What is the ratio \(AF:FD?\)

solutions.text:
Applying the Angle Bisector Theorem to \(\triangle ABC\) gives \(BD:DC=AB:AC=6:8,\) so \(BD=\dfrac{6}{6+8}\cdot 7=3.\)

Now \(BF\) lies along the bisector of \(\angle ABD\) in \(\triangle ABD,\) so by the Angle Bisector Theorem again, \[ \begin{gathered} AF:FD=AB:BD\\ =6:3=2:1. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Apply the Angle Bisector Theorem in \(\triangle ABC\) to find \(BD\)
In \(\triangle ABD,\) segment \(BF\) bisects \(\angle ABD,\) so \(AF:FD=AB:BD\)
